sample_unit: patients (Parkinson's disease participants across two public datasets: Figshare n=35, DAPHNET n=10)

links.outcome: Performance gap between laboratory-trained and daily-living datasets (dataset shift) in FoG detection F1
links.effect: Laboratory F1 reached 0.9999 ± 0.0002, whereas daily living F1 dropped to 0.55 ± 0.26 (p < 0.0001), an 83% gap with a 1299-fold increase in variance.
links.quote: Most importantly, cross-dataset validation revealed an 83% performance gap: laboratory F1 reached 0.9999 ± 0.0002, whereas daily living F1 dropped to 0.55 ± 0.26 (p < 0.0001), with a 1299-fold increase in variance.

links.outcome: Overestimated performance on laboratory data versus real-world data
links.effect: Laboratory F1 0.9999 versus daily living F1 0.55; laboratory success does not guarantee real-world utility.
links.quote: These findings demonstrate that laboratory success does not guarantee real-world utility.

unlisted_practices: F1-based versus AUC-based early stopping during model training (F1 0.55 vs 0.37, p = 0.0008)

screen.reason: Evaluates temporal convolutional network performance across lab vs daily living wearable datasets to analyze the cross-dataset performance gap; tests model training strategies rather than clinical deployment practices or guardrails.
